sources.title: A. G. Basden, C. A. Haniff, C. D. Mackay, Photon counting strategies with low-light-level CCDs, MNRAS 345, 985-991 (2003)
sources.locator: output probability distribution of the multiplication register (gamma form for n input electrons), section 2; arXiv:astro-ph/0307305
supports: the high-gain EMCCD register output for n > 0 input electrons as Gamma(shape n, scale G), mean G n, variance G^2 n
zero input gives zero output; thresholding strategies only matter at photon-counting flux
limitations: a high-gain approximation; finite-stage moments at intermediate gain need D2's model
in-register (serial) CIC is not covered by this model and is outside the claim

sources.title: M. S. Robbins and B. J. Hadwen, The noise performance of electron multiplying charge-coupled devices, IEEE Transactions on Electron Devices 50(5), 1227-1232 (2003)
sources.locator: excess-noise factor F^2 = 2(G-1)G^-(N+1)/N + 1/G and its high-gain limit 2; DOI and pages from the implementer's knowledge and the planning prompt, not verified in the implementing session
supports: the excess noise factor of an EMCCD register approaches F^2 = 2 at high gain
the finite-stage value at 536 stages and G >= 100 is about 1.97, within 2 % of the Gamma approximation (decision D00-13)
limitations: bibliographic details taken from the planning prompt; a web search confirmed the paper and its sqrt(2) result through citing work but did not return the DOI

sources.title: J. R. Janesick, Photon Transfer DN -> lambda, SPIE Press PM170 (2007)
sources.locator: photon transfer: conversion gain, read noise, fixed-pattern noise and PRNU chapters
supports: conversion gain in electrons per DN, read noise in electrons, PRNU as a relative photoresponse map, fixed-pattern offsets
limitations: a method reference, not a specification of any preset's values

sources.title: S. Thomas, T. Fusco, A. Tokovinin, M. Nicolle, V. Michau, G. Rousset, Comparison of centroid computation algorithms in a Shack-Hartmann sensor, MNRAS 371, 323-336 (2006)
sources.locator: sections 2.1-2.3 (definitions, spot profiles, error decomposition; pp. 324-325), 3.1 (equations 11-13; p. 326), 3.2 (equation 14; pp. 326-327), 4.1 (thresholding; p. 328), Appendix A (p. 335) and Appendix B (pp. 335-336); read in the publisher's PDF
supports: method reference for centre-of-gravity noise: section 3.1 gives the photon- and read-noise contributions for a Gaussian spot (equations 11-12, after Rousset 1999; equation 11 also assumes Nyquist sampling) and, for a diffraction-limited spot under photon noise, a photon-noise variance that increases linearly with the lenslet field of view (equation 13, derived in Appendix A); with read noise the paper states that the noise does not depend on the spot structure

centre-of-gravity response: linear for an infinite field of view and adequate sampling, non-linear when the field is small compared with the spot (section 3.2; equation 14 and Appendix B give the finite-window estimate for a Gaussian spot)
a comparison of the plain centre of gravity with thresholded, weighted, correlation and quad-cell estimators; the repository implements the plain and the thresholded centre of gravity
limitations: the implemented models use none of the paper's closed-form expressions, Gaussian or diffraction-limited: detector.noise_model and detector.validity contract the exact per-pixel Jacobian of the plain centre of gravity over the declared finite window, which applies to any expected spot inside the model's support domain (assumption ledger row B14) and carries the window dependence through each pixel's lever arm

that a thresholded or minimum-subtracted centre of gravity lies outside the first-order noise model is the repository's own support rule (detector.noise_model reports it unsupported); the paper instead evaluates the thresholded centre of gravity's noise approximately with equations 11-12, N_s^2 being the average number of pixels above threshold, and notes that the threshold must be subtracted to keep a unit response (section 4.1); the repository does not adopt that approximation

the sections, equations and appendices above were read in the publisher's PDF on 2026-10-20, consistent with the GPT pre-refactor audit's reading of a coauthor-uploaded copy (2026-10-17); this entry restates no formula of the paper, and the implementation uses none

sources.title: J. B. Oke and J. E. Gunn, Secondary standard stars for absolute spectrophotometry, ApJ 266, 713-717 (1983)
sources.locator: AB system definition m_AB = -2.5 log10 f_nu - 48.60 (cgs); bibcode 1983ApJ...266..713O
supports: AB zero point f_nu,0 = 10^-19.44 erg s^-1 cm^-2 Hz^-1 = 3630.78 Jy (rounded 3631 Jy)
limitations: the absolute calibration of the Oke standards was later revised by about 0.04 mag; irrelevant to a synthetic magnitude scale

sources.title: EMVA Standard 1288, Release 4.0 Linear: Standard for characterization of image sensors and cameras
sources.locator: sections 2-4: photon/electron units, overall system gain, saturation capacity versus digital saturation, PRNU and DSNU
supports: linear-camera units: photons, electrons, DN, gain K
limitations: its linear independent-noise model does not establish EMCCD or coupled-pixel validity

sources.title: A. Kannawadi, C. A. Shapiro, R. Mandelbaum, C. M. Hirata, J. W. Kruk, J. D. Rhodes, The impact of interpixel capacitance in CMOS detectors on PSF shapes and implications for WFIRST, PASP 128, 095001 (2016)
sources.locator: IPC as a linear 3x3 kernel acting on collected charge, and its effect on noise covariance and PSF shapes
supports: a nonnegative unit-sum 3x3 electronic coupling kernel K and the covariance K diag(mu) K^T of coupled Poisson signals
limitations: describes CMOS/HgCdTe interpixel capacitance; applying K to an EMCCD after the register is a declared synthetic placement, not a property of EMCCDs

sources.title: STScI STIS Data Handbook, chapter 3.4 (calibration steps) and the Astropy CCD reduction guide, calibrating dark images
sources.locator: bias, dark and flat corrected products and propagated errors; https://www.astropy.org/ccd-reduction-and-photometry-guide/v/2.0.0/notebooks/03-05-Calibrate-dark-images.html
supports: master bias, bias-subtracted master dark scaled to the exposure, flat normalized over valid pixels
propagation of master errors into processed images
limitations: method references only, not validation against instrument data

sources.title: S. Gladysz and R. Rebolo, The E-ELT Design Reference Mission: Direct imaging of terrestrial and giant exoplanets (DRM report S3, v2)
supports: a separate SCAO case: spatially filtered SH 84x84, 2 ms integration, 6 ms readout-plus-reconstruction lag, 3 e- read noise, 0.6-0.9 um sensing, 30 nm NCPA
limitations: PAOLA-based analytic method with 0.7 arcsec seeing, its own pupil and perfect spatial filtering
its lag definition differs from the R1 delayed-command convention; values are not merged into the normative case

sources.title: C. Bechet and M. Tallon, Reducing the Fractal Iterative Method (FRiM) to the cost of half an iteration, ESO RTC workshop 2012
supports: an independent FRiM/OCTOPUS SCAO experiment: 42 m, obstruction 0.28, 500 Hz, nine layers, r0 = 0.129 m, tau0 = 2.8 ms, ground DM 85x85, one NGS, SH 84x84, 1e5 photons/frame/subaperture
limitations: slides, not a complete reproducible input deck or a raw SCAO PSF dataset
its nine-layer profile is not the packaged ten-layer R1 profile; substituting one for the other is not a reproduction

reference_cases.why_not_runnable: analytic PAOLA study with a different atmosphere, pupil, filtering, noise and lag convention; no end-to-end input deck
the nine-layer profile, noise model and reconstruction details are not published in reproducible form
